import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a bar plot to visualize survival rate by sex and passenger class
# 'survived' is 0 or 1, so the mean directly represents the survival rate
sns.barplot(data=df, x='sex', y='survived', hue='class', palette='viridis', errorbar=None)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Survival Rate on Titanic by Sex and Passenger Class', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sex', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)
plt.legend(title='Passenger Class', title_fontsize='11', fontsize='10')
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Ensure layout is tight and save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a bar plot to visualize survival rate by sex and passenger class
# 'survived' is 0 or 1, so the mean directly represents the survival rate
sns.barplot(data=df, x='sex', y='survived', hue='class', palette='viridis', errorbar=None)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Survival Rate on Titanic by Sex and Passenger Class', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sex', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)
plt.legend(title='Passenger Class', title_fontsize='11', fontsize='10')
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Ensure layout is tight and save the figure
